newsitem.title: USA: New stock offerings look set for another strong week.
newsitem.headline: New stock offerings look set for another strong week.

text.p: New stock offerings could be poised for strong gains this week after a stellar showing last week and a record-setting bull run in the stock market.

Last week saw a record number of dollars raised in initial public offerings and analysts are predicting a similar whirlwind this week. About 20 deals are on deck, including two Chinese firms listing stock on this side of the Pacific.
"It was a great week for IPOs, and a great week for Goldman Sachs," said Tom Tuft, co-chief operating officer of Equity Capital Markets at that firm.

Goldman led the market debuts of Santa Fe International Inc. and Polo Ralph Lauren Corp., the largest and second biggest deals so far in 1997. Goldman also led Hartford Life Inc.'s April IPO, the No. 3 public offering of 1997.
"It's a very good environment for IPOs right now, particularly for good companies," Tuft said.
Other IPO analysts say because many deals were postponed in April when demand was scant, the market was able to weed out lower quality deals, leaving better firms on the menu.

Helped by the two large deals, last week was the top grossing week for IPOs so far in 1997. Thirteen offerings raised $2.65 billion, a stunning 967 percent more than in the previous week, according to MCM Corporatewatch.
This week, 25 IPOs are on deck to raise $2.3 billion. ARM Financial Group Inc., Qwest Telecommunications and Genesys Telecommunications are among them.
Qwest, founded in 1988, is building a nationwide fiber optic network for phone, fax, paging and multimedia communications that piggybacks on existing railroad systems.
Qwest is offering 11.5 million shares to price between $17 and $20 in an IPO to be led by Salomon Brothers.
Software application company Genesys will offer two million of the 2.5 million shares to be sold in its IPO, led by Goldman Sachs.
ARM Financial, which provides asset management services, will offer 5.75 million shares for $12-$14 each.
Two Hong Kong offerings could reap rewards as investors grab a chance to invest in China, according to John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

Plastics and resins-maker Beijing Yanua Petrochemical Co. Ltd. will offer 9.1 million ADRs for between $10.99 and $14.65 each. Peak International Ltd., which supplies products that handle semiconductor chips, will offer three million shares for $12 to $14 each.

The largest deal due this week is the privatisation of Portugal's national electric company Electricidad de Portugal. Thirty percent of EDP will be sold in a global offering of 150 million shares expected to price at $20.53 to $26.39 each, according to the prospectus.
Boston Properties Inc., a real estate investment trust owned by Mort Zuckerman, has filed to raise $737.5 million in an offering of 29.5 million shares for about $25 each.
